questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Meaning and Characteristics of Business' refers to.
questions.a: Business refers to those economic activities that are concerned with the production or purchase and sale of goods or supply of services with the main objective of earning profit.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Meaning and Characteristics of Business'.
questions.a: Business is a human economic activity involving production, exchange, and sale of goods and services undertaken regularly for profit.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'Meaning and Characteristics of Business'.
questions.a: Define business and list its main characteristics.

concepts.title: Comparison of Business, Profession and Employment

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Comparison of Business, Profession and Employment' refers to.
questions.a: Business is an economic activity for profit through production or trade; profession is an occupation requiring specialised knowledge and service for a fee; employment is work performed under a contract for a salary or wage.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Comparison of Business, Profession and Employment'.
questions.a: Business, profession, and employment are three types of economic activities differing in capital, risk, reward, qualification, and transfer of interest.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'Comparison of Business, Profession and Employment'.
questions.a: Distinguish between business, profession, and employment.

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Objectives of Business' refers to.
questions.a: Objectives of business are the goals that a business seeks to achieve through its operations, including economic, social, personal, and national objectives.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Objectives of Business'.
questions.a: Profit is the primary economic objective but a business must also pursue social and personal objectives to survive and grow.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'Objectives of Business'.
questions.a: What are the main objectives of business?

concepts.title: Classification of Business Activities: Industry and Commerce

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Classification of Business Activities: Industry and Commerce' refers to.
questions.a: Business activities are broadly classified into industry, concerned with production or processing of goods, and commerce, concerned with the distribution of goods and services.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Classification of Business Activities: Industry and Commerce'.
questions.a: All business activities are either industry (production side) or commerce (distribution side), and commerce further includes trade and auxiliaries.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'Classification of Business Activities: Industry and Commerce'.
questions.a: Classify business activities into industry and commerce.

concepts.title: Types of Industries: Primary, Secondary and Tertiary

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Types of Industries: Primary, Secondary and Tertiary' refers to.
questions.a: Primary industries extract or raise resources from nature, secondary industries process or manufacture goods from raw materials, and tertiary industries provide services supporting production and distribution.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Types of Industries: Primary, Secondary and Tertiary'.
questions.a: Industries are classified by activity into primary (extractive), secondary (manufacturing and construction), and tertiary (service) sectors.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'Types of Industries: Primary, Secondary and Tertiary'.
questions.a: Explain the three types of industries with examples.

concepts.title: Commerce: Trade and Auxiliaries to Trade

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Commerce: Trade and Auxiliaries to Trade' refers to.
questions.a: Commerce is the sum of trade and auxiliaries to trade, where trade is the buying and selling of goods and auxiliaries are services that assist trade such as transport, banking, insurance, warehousing, and advertising.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Commerce: Trade and Auxiliaries to Trade'.
questions.a: Commerce connects producers and consumers through trade (exchange) and auxiliaries (supporting services) that remove barriers of place, time, risk, finance, and information.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'Commerce: Trade and Auxiliaries to Trade'.
questions.a: Define commerce and explain its components.

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Business Risk: Meaning and Nature' refers to.
questions.a: Business risk is the probability of loss or insufficient profit caused by unfavourable events or uncertainties that affect business operations.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Business Risk: Meaning and Nature'.
questions.a: Business risk arises from uncertainties and is characterised by uncertainty of return, which is an essential feature of every business.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'Business Risk: Meaning and Nature'.
questions.a: What is business risk?

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Causes of Business Risk' refers to.
questions.a: Business risk arises from natural causes such as floods and earthquakes, human causes such as negligence and dishonesty, economic causes such as market and price changes, and other causes such as political and technological changes.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Causes of Business Risk'.
questions.a: The main causes of business risk are natural, human, economic, and other causes including political, technological, and physical causes.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'Causes of Business Risk'.
questions.a: Explain the causes of business risk.

questions.q: Using the method 'Role of Profit in Business', work with: fixed_cost = 80000, price_per_unit = 25, units_sold = 100, variable_cost = 8000. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of profit.
questions.a: -85500 rupees

questions.q: Take the relation taught for 'Role of Profit in Business' and work with: fixed_cost = 5000, price_per_unit = 12, units_sold = 100, variable_cost = 500. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of profit.
questions.a: -4300 rupees

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Role of Profit in Business' refers to.
questions.a: Profit is the surplus of revenue over costs and acts as a source of income, a measure of efficiency, a means of survival and growth, and a reward for risk-bearing in business.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Role of Profit in Business'.
questions.a: Profit is essential for business survival, growth, and innovation, and it acts as the reward for bearing business risk.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Role of Profit in Business', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: Profit = Total Revenue - Total Cost
